requirements.requirement: Run a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster on node1, node2, node3 holding application data
requirements.summary: node1 bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster reaching cluster_size=1/Primary; node2 and node3 sequentially joined and reached Synced state with cluster_size incrementing to 2 then 3. An application database (appdb.orders) was created on node1 with 3 rows and confirmed present identically on node2 and node3, demonstrating a healthy 3-node cluster holding application data.

requirements.requirement: Add node4 as a fourth member that carries the data that already exists
requirements.summary: node4 was configured with the same Galera cluster address including all four nodes, started, and joined via SST reaching cluster_size=4/Synced. A SELECT on node4 immediately after joining showed all 3 pre-existing rows from appdb.orders present, confirming data was carried over.

requirements.requirement: node4 should accept writes like the other members
requirements.summary: An INSERT executed directly on node4 was immediately visible in a follow-up SELECT on node4, and the same new row was independently confirmed present on node1, node2, and node3 via SELECT queries, demonstrating node4 accepts writes that replicate cluster-wide.

overall_summary: The three material outcomes of the task — a healthy 3-node Galera cluster holding application data, node4 joining as a fourth member that receives the existing data, and node4 accepting writes that replicate to the rest of the cluster — are all directly and clearly demonstrated in the captured evidence. Separately, the mandated provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was executed cleanly on all four nodes: each shows a distinct pre-restart boot_id, a systemctl reboot acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot_id (cross-checked against the fixed after-prepare and after-executor lifecycle snapshots), and full recovery to Synced/cluster_size=4 with the row count intact, with restarts performed sequentially to preserve quorum. This restart evidence is high quality but is supplemental to (not part of) the public task contract, so it does not itself gate the requirement statuses above.
limitations: The application user's password was generated and redacted/deleted rather than captured, so end-to-end authentication as appuser (versus the sudo-local mysql client) was not directly observed, though this is a minor implementation detail not central to the stated task outcomes.

One config approach (a separate galera-cluster.cnf drop-in) failed and was reverted before a working configuration was applied; this is noted as a bounded, self-corrected hygiene item rather than a task failure.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations map directly to task requirements (package installs, /etc/hosts entries, firewall ports, galera.cnf edits, cluster bootstrap/join, restarts). Two minor issues were observed. First, an initial attempt to enable Galera via a separate drop-in file /etc/my.cnf.d/galera-cluster.cnf (cmd-f159f62d5309401a on node1, cmd-ed2176e89471454a on node2, cmd-82e07b1bc3cb40ec on node3) failed to take effect (wsrep stayed OFF, cluster_size=0/Disconnected per cmd-f4f6e1a573e54b21 and cmd-0d2e13269f124d62) because it was shadowed by galera.cnf's wsrep_on=0; the executor corrected course by deleting that file and directly sed-editing galera.cnf (cmd-302d2afde2de4048, cmd-97628fe2476144b7, cmd-fb79f79178084dc2). This was a bounded, non-destructive troubleshooting mutation that was fully reverted before the working configuration was applied. Second, the executor installed policycoreutils-python-utils on node1 to check SELinux port contexts (cmd-473e6a2e4f9642cc) even though it discovered mysqld_port_t already covered the needed ports; this diagnostic install left a retained but low-risk package. Third, install/reboot log residue (/tmp/install.log, /tmp/install.pid, /tmp/reboot.log) was left on all four nodes per the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; these are low-risk artifacts of legitimate install/restart commands rather than unrelated mutations. No failed services, unsafe exposure, or damaged package state were observed after the run.
